The user's contact line is metal < 1 mm (CLAUDE.md, reaffirmed 2026-10-17), but the plain verified gap that now decides counts taken poses with metal at 0-1 mm as taken. Metal hugs the skin overhead, which is the user's first priority. Of the 8 taken overhead workspace poses (elev >= 140), all 8 have metal under 3 mm, 6 under 2 mm and 1 under 1 mm; held out it is 17 of 17, 12 and 3. The overhead per-pose floor p10 is 1.40 mm (held out 1.05). Over all taken poses this design is better than the lead: 130 of 367 (35 %) have metal under 3 mm against 178 of 371 (48 %), and the 1-2 mm shell holds 12.04 points (lead 15.12). The pattern is shared by every knuckle row, so it is a gap between the score and the goal, not a gamed number.

K is scored at its slaved value. One clock-spring cap keeps the bell-crank follower on the hub-2 lobe, and K sits on stop A (dK = 0) on 227 of 367 taken bench poses (62 %) and 534 of 853 held-out poses (63 %). No spring-hold check (judge R17 or a posture sweep under gravity) is on file for this design, so the unpowered MVP1 tracking of K rests on an unmeasured spring. The kinematic bench cannot show whether the follower lifts or K lags.
